title: Writing Simple Sentences
introduction: Practise writing simple sentences with familiar words and short sentences.
definition: A simple sentence can tell who or what it is about and what happens or what it is like.
rules: Build a simple sentence with a subject and a verb. Add an object or description when needed.
Use a capital letter at the beginning, spaces between words and punctuation at the end.
Practise writing about different themes: school, food, family, animals, hobbies and weather.

examples.question: Arrange: likes / Aina / mangoes.
steps: Start with the person, then the action and object.

examples.question: Arrange: can / jump / Rabbits.
steps: Use the base verb after can.

examples.question: Write a sentence about your schoolbag using has.
steps: Use has to describe a feature.

exercises.question: Put in order: like / I / rice
Put in order: is / The cup / blue
Put in order: jump / can / We
Put in order: a kite / has / Ali
Put in order: are / The books / new
Put in order: my / This is / bag
Put in order: drinks / Mei / milk
Put in order: play / They / football
Put in order: The dog / under the table / sleeps
exercises.answer: The dog sleeps under the table.
exercises.solution: Answer: The dog sleeps under the table.

summary: A simple sentence can tell who or what it is about and what happens or what it is like.
